standard_prerequisites.name: The two criteria for a ring to be J-2: the condition on finite purely inseparable extensions of residue fields, and the condition on finite ring extensions being J-1
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Lemma \ref{lemma-J-2}, cited at proof lines 11959-11960, 11978-11979, and 11987-11988
standard_prerequisites.use: Provide the criterion that is verified for each of the seven classes.

standard_prerequisites.name: The integral closure of a one-dimensional Nagata domain in a finite extension is a normal domain of dimension one, hence regular
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-integral-dim-up} and Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-criterion-normal}, cited at proof lines 11968-11971
standard_prerequisites.use: Settle the case of a minimal prime in a one-dimensional Nagata ring.

standard_prerequisites.name: A finite extension of a complete local ring is a product of complete local rings
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-quotient-complete-local}, cited at proof lines 11980-11981
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the complete local case to the case of a domain via the regular-locus criterion.

standard_prerequisites.name: A Noetherian complete local domain is J-0, and regularity is preserved when the regular locus meets every closed subset in a nonempty open subset
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Lemma \ref{lemma-complete-Noetherian-domain-J-0} and Lemma \ref{lemma-intersection-regular-with-closed}, cited at proof lines 11982-11984

core_obligations: Reduce the cases of fields, the integers, Nagata rings of dimension one and characteristic-zero Dedekind domains to the residue field criterion (proof lines 11959-11961).
Verify that criterion for a one-dimensional Nagata ring, splitting into the maximal and the minimal prime case and using finiteness of the integral closure (proof lines 11961-11972).
Reduce the complete local case to the criterion on finite extensions and to the J-0 statement for complete local domains (proof lines 11978-11984).
Settle the one-dimensional local case by noting that finite extensions have finite spectrum and that the regular locus is stable under generalisation (proof lines 11986-11990).
proof_roadmap: Residue field criterion for the first group of cases (proof lines 11959-11972).
Complete local rings via finite extensions and the J-0 statement (proof lines 11978-11984).
One-dimensional local rings via stability of the regular locus (proof lines 11986-11990).
difficulty_reason: The proposition collects seven classes of rings that are J-2. The proof checks the relevant criterion for each class: for fields, the integers, one-dimensional Nagata rings and Dedekind domains with fraction field of characteristic zero it verifies the condition on finite purely inseparable extensions of residue fields, carrying out the one-dimensional Nagata case in detail, where either the prime is maximal, so the extension is finite over a regular ring, or it is minimal, where the Nagata condition makes the integral closure in the extension finite and hence a one-dimensional normal, therefore regular, domain. For complete local rings and for one-dimensional local rings it uses the criterion on finite extensions instead, reducing the first to the statement that a complete local domain is J-0 and observing in the second case that the regular locus is stable under generalisation on a finite spectrum.
